rationale: Evidence from iteration 10 (score 931.1, best so far): every trial finished on all three development tracks (oval 20/20 at 2.11 s, s-bend 20/20 at 2.44 s, slalom 20/20 at 2.65 s). Mean rms_error is 0.007 to 0.016 m, and steering oscillation is 0.20 to 0.35. The score gap to the maximum now comes from three terms. Line-loss events are about 1.0 per trial on every track, which costs about 15 points each through 120*(1 - LL/8). Completion time costs about 18 points on the time term (60*(1 - t/3)). The rms term is already near its ceiling. Iteration 5 showed that cutting base_speed hurt, and iterations 4 to 10 did not show that raising kp or kd helps, so I am not changing gains. Geometry is already at the contract minimum for mass (0.4 kg) and body_length (0.10 m), which is the lever that made the slalom finish. Change: base_speed 1.5 to 1.55, a small step toward the time term. It should cut about 0.05 to 0.1 s on each track, worth about 1 to 2 points per track. Everything else is held fixed (geometry, weights, kp 3.0, ki 0.05, kd 1.2, last_direction) so the effect of speed can be read cleanly. Risk: the final track is unseen, so a faster robot might leave the line on a sharper bend. Expected result: all tracks still finish 20/20, completion time about 0.05 to 0.1 s lower, and score about 932 to 934 on the development tracks. Hypotheses: (a) if any track drops below 20/20 finishes or slalom off-track exits return, revert to base_speed 1.5, which is the measured best; (b) if line_loss_events stay near 1.0, the event is probably a start or sensor-reach artefact, not speed, and the next step is to test sensor y back to 0.06 for a 0.5 LL reduction at the cost of some phase lead; (c) if completion_time falls with no added losses, base_speed 1.6 would be the next test. Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, and controller_errors.
